  here is an exploratory reference by independent readers. It is not a frozen ruler until Alex signs it, and it is labelled as such
  in every result.
- **Data.** The Flash K6b draw-1 forward run over 115 gold articles (`poc/data/clean-step1-takeover-2026-11-07/gold-k6b-flash/`):
  282 kept items with summaries, passages, party, dates, tier and thesis links, in forward order.
- **Out of scope.** Step 3's writer, Step 4, the UI, frozen production files.
- **Budget.** Embeddings (`text-embedding-3-small`) and Jev ($0.042 per M input tokens). Calls and cost are counted before any send.

## 1. Council A (independent design, then one challenge round)

The fresh Codex session is `01a1b870…`; its records are `council/a-handoff.md`, `a-codex.md`, `a-claude.md` and `b-*.md`. Agreed
design:

- **Reference pairs (exploratory, model-authored, labelled as such).**
  - Population: ordered pairs (earlier item, later item) from different articles, with availability set by forward article order.
    Same-article pairs are excluded. An item linked to two theses is one item, queried once per {thesis, evidence} association.
  - Candidate pairs come from routes that do not use the embedding search under test:
    - shared figures;
    - shared parties and named entities;
    - summary-word Jaccard;
    - same-thesis lexical rank.
  - Readers do not see which route found a pair, nor any search or model output.
  - Labels:
    - repeat;
    - revision;
    - same quantity, different party (a subtype of different);
    - different;
    - insufficient information;
    - and, for repeats, whether the later item is richer or qualified (D204's risk).

    Two blind readers label each pair with the same full source context; disagreements are kept, then adjudicated with the source.
- **Generator-miss control.**
  - Sample: 30 incoming items, drawn uniformly within three time strata (articles 1–40, 41–80, 81–115) with a fixed seed. Inclusion
    probabilities are recorded and the estimate weighted.
  - Scan: the reader reads the incoming item's full passages, then every earlier summary.
  - Audit: a random sample of unflagged pairs is re-checked with full context.
  - Expected to be inconclusive if positives are few; expand rather than claim.
- **Retrieval arms.**
  - R0: production as written, word overlap within the linked thesis, top 10; a new thesis has no candidates.
  - R0e: entity-wide word overlap.
  - R1: embedding of summary, verified passages, party, time and period; query of thesis description, outcome and period plus the
    incoming summary and passages; entity-wide; top 10.
  - R2: R1 without the thesis in the query.
  - Strict forward availability throughout.
- **Comparison.** Jev with the cross-thesis wording and full fields, tested first on the labelled pairs, apart from retrieval, then on
  the retrieved candidates. An uncertainty option is open; an uncertain pair is never silently called different.
- **Metrics.**
  - recall at 10 by type and by cross-thesis status;
  - the Jev confusion matrix;
  - false repeats by cause, over true-different and over predicted repeats;
  - the combined path (right target and right label);
  - the dossier per thesis before and after dedup, labelled a simulation.

  The 90% figures are discussion targets until Alex agrees.
- **Open for Alex:** what is saved when one item is a repeat of one candidate and a revision of another, or a repeat of several.

**Dossiers fixed before retrieval** (Flash d1 thesis ids):
1. Customer financing and backstops: clean-1, the revenue-sharing and credit-support model.
2. Competition: clean-18 (custom silicon and AMD) and clean-24 (inference-chip challengers).
3. Product roadmap: clean-11 (Vera Rubin volume shipping) and clean-17 (Kyber).

## 2. Reference (2026-11-07/08)

- **v1** (`reference.json`, kept as history): 573 pairs, from 488 triage-possible pairs, 66 scan-flagged pairs and a 60-pair audit.
  - Two blind readers agreed on 94.9%; a third settled 29 disputes.
  - Readers marked 313 of 397 "repeats" as richer. A hand-check of 6 found 2 that were not repeats.
- **v2** (`reference-v2.json`, council round 1): two fresh readers answered two separate questions, the relation and the material the
  later item adds, over 497 pairs (all v1 positives, 60 sampled negatives, 6 insufficient).
  - Relation agreement 93.4%; 24 of the 33 disputes were between same statement and different fact of the same matter.
  - Result: same_statement 333, different_fact_same_matter 105, revision 25, same quantity other party 8, different 24, insufficient 2.
  - All 60 v1 "repeats" were relabelled as different facts.
  - My hand-read of 18 same_statement pairs: 2 clearly wrong (NVL144 against NVL576), 2 arguable.
- **v3 additions** (`v3-answer-E/F-*`): the 48 never-labelled pairs Jev called repeats on the product path or in the forward
  simulation, two readers.
  - 24 same statement, 17 different fact, 1 other party, 6 disputed.
  - So the reference had missed about half of those pairs, and Jev was wrong on the other half.

## 3. Search: recall at 10 (`score_retrieval_v2.py`, forward simulation)

| Query | Per association, raw history (391) | Deduplicated history | Forward simulation, real Jev decisions |
|---|---|---|---|
| R0, production, within thesis | 82.1% | | |
| R0e, word overlap, entity-wide | 78.5% | | |
| R1, thesis + evidence (agreed) | 90.0% | 125/125 | 112/113 |
| R2, evidence only | 95.9% | 113/113 | |

- Revisions: R1 found 22 of 25.
- Cross-thesis positives: only 3, so no conclusion can be drawn on cross-thesis search.
- The raw-history misses come from many copies of the same story crowding the top 10; merging removes that crowding.
- 112/113 counts only known matches, from one Jev draw.

## 4. Comparison (Jev)

**Pair level on the labelled pairs** (`score_jev.py`):

| Arm | Agreement | Wrong merges |
|---|---|---|
| J0, production question | 82.4% | 30 (9.4%; 14 from one bundle record) |
| J1, cross-thesis wording | 80.8% | 22 (7.5%) |

Pair level is not the verdict. A record is saved or discarded whole, and one true match is enough.

**Product path, per incoming record** (`score_product_path.py`; J0 over the R1 top 10):

| Arm | Merged into a true same statement | No true match | Duplicates kept |
|---|---|---|---|
| J0 | 106 | 6 | 4 |
| J1 | 97 | 2 | 13 |

**Forward simulation** (`forward_sim.py`, J0, article order, the library each decision would see): 282 items become 180 records.
- 102 merged.
- Both loss readers say 93 of those have a true same-statement home. 9 do not: by my read, 3 clear (Sharon AI into Firmus; analysts' 82%
  and 41% into the analysts' revenue-doubling record; NVL576 into NVL144) and 6 arguable.
- 10 cite the incoming source on an extra record that the incoming record does not state.
- 14 true repeats in the results were left unmerged.

## 5. What merging loses (`loss-answer-G/H-*`, all 102 merged items, two readers)

- Both readers say a material fact is lost that no other record holds in 66 of 102 (agreement 93/102). The readers over-flag.
- My hand-read of a random 12 of the 66:
  - 3 material: Q1 net income, EPS and margin; Q2 guidance "±2%, assumes no China data-centre revenue"; the Taiwan raid on Supermicro
    bundled into a Singapore record;
  - 3 moderate;
  - 6 trivial.
- A random 4 of the no-loss items: 4 had no loss.
- This is a small diagnostic sample, not a population estimate.
- **Mechanism:**
  - Step 1 records carry one matter, often several facts.
  - Later articles retell a statement and add figures or qualifications.
  - The current rule keeps only the earlier text and adds the source, so those additions are discarded.

**Probe J2** (`jev-J2-merges.json`, $0.004): same_statement only when the incoming record adds nothing an analyst would keep.
- Merges fell from 102 to 22 on the same 102 merges. This is not a new forward run.
- All 3 material and all 3 moderate losses were kept, but so were 5 of 6 trivial and 3 of 4 no-loss items.
- Jev cannot separate trivial from material additions any better than the readers can, so a materiality gate either loses facts or
  undoes most of the merging.

## 6. Council B (rounds 1–3: `council/c-*`, `d-*`, `e-*`)

- Round 1: re-label with two separate questions, and score per association.
- Round 2: do not claim that search passes or that detection is close. Run a forward simulation and read every merged record against the
  dossier.
- Round 3: grouping preserves text, but has not been shown to be understood by the judge.
  - Say "same statement", not "same story".
  - J2's 22 is not a forward run.
  - Group membership with several matches still needs a rule.

## 7. Verdict and the question for Alex (2026-11-08)

The hypothesis "top-10 search plus Jev repeat/revision/different, then source-only merging" is contradicted on the merge action, so the
line stops (D355).

- Search is not the bottleneck.
- Detection is near but not at the proposed line: 3 to 9 wrong merges in 102, and 14 duplicates in 113.
- Source-only merging discards facts in a noticeable share of merges.

Question for Alex: when a later article repeats a stored statement with more detail, what does the library do?
- **(A) Recommended:** keep the later record's text and source inside the stored record's group. The original is not rewritten, and the
  judge reads the group as one statement.
- **(B)** Merge only exact retellings.
- **(C)** Keep source-only merging.

The proposed pass lines and the conflict rule for several matches are still not confirmed.

**Next test if (A):** build the groups on the forward history, show the judge's input for the three predeclared dossiers before and
after, and check that grouped details are visible and that nothing is counted twice. The Kyber group of 14 retellings is the size case.
Then take the next class: wrong groups and missed repeats.

**Cost:** Jev about $0.19 in all (labelled $0.021, product path $0.116, forward $0.054, J2 $0.004, at the listed rate). Embeddings
earlier. Readers were Codex read-only sessions.

## 8. Log rows

| Arm | Hypothesis | Change | Result | Kept |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 against R0 | An entity-wide embedding finds cross-thesis repeats | Embedding query with thesis + evidence | 90.0% against 82.1% per association; 112/113 in the forward run | yes (agreed design) |
| J1 against J0 | Removing the "same thesis" premise reduces wrong merges | Cross-thesis wording | Fewer wrong merges (2 against 6 per record), more duplicates (13 against 4) | open |
| J2 | A stricter repeat removes the loss | same_statement requires nothing new | Loss removed; merges 102 → 22; trivial retellings kept | no: refuted as a gate; it motivates grouping |

## 9. Alex's decision (2026-11-08)

On the question in §7, Alex replied: "A 继续；跑council loop 开始做". **Decided:** each repeat's own text and source are kept inside the
stored record's group, and the original is not rewritten. Recorded in the clean PRD, §5 repeat handoff and §6. Still not confirmed:
the Step 2 pass lines, and the rule for several matches.

## 10. Grouping round (2026-11-08, council loop)

**Frame.** Alex chose A (§9).
- Goal: build grouping and test whether readers notice what later reports add, without double counting or being misled, compared with
  source-only merging and with no merging (the full-information control).
- No model judge exists (PRD §7), so blind readers act as the dossier's readers.

**Council A** (`council/group/a-*`, `b-*`).
- Agreed:
  - the group contract: the original is never rewritten; members keep their own id, text, fields and source; links carry their
    provenance; revisions are links; a replay is idempotent; one unit per item; distinct articles are counted;
  - the dossier view;
  - three views built from one stored history;
  - a key written by independent readers before any view is read;
  - one view per reader.
- Settled in the challenge:
  - several matches (15 items): kept as their own entry with `also_matches` references in both merged views. This is a **test
    convention only**; the product rule stays Alex's.
  - What was built: the isolated library with only the decided rows, refusing a failed comparison and several targets.

**Built.**
- `clean-arch/step3/library.py`: groups, members, links, revisions, refusals and the dossier text.
- `test_library.py`: 12 tests, one per table row. All 5 mutants were caught (the original rewritten, a replay appended, articles not
  distinct, a failed comparison saved, several targets joined).
- `build_views.py` replays the forward simulation's 282 stored decisions through the library: 195 groups, 0 refused. This is a
  fixed-decision reconstruction, not a new forward run.

**Reader test** (`reader-test/`).
- Questions and scoring rules were frozen first (`FROZEN.sha256`, checked by the scorer): 39 questions over three dossiers.
- Key: two readers; a third settled the 16 questions where the drafts differed.
- 18 masked view readers; 3 blind graders. Tally: `score_reader_test.py`, 234 grades.

| Dossier | Detail: none / source / group (out of 12) | Unsupported claims: none / source / group | Characters: none / source / group |
|---|---|---|---|
| financing | 7.0 / 1.0 / 6.5 | 0 / 4 / 0 | 43.7k / 23.0k / 42.5k |
| competition | 7.5 / 2.0 / 8.0 | 2 / 2 / 2 | 18.1k / 15.2k / 22.5k |
| roadmap | 10.5 / 0.0 / 10.5 | 2 / 0 / 0 | 62.9k / 40.2k / 65.9k |

- Detail in total: none 25, source 3, group 25, out of 36.
- Double counting: 0 in every view, on 4 independence questions.
- Controls, comparison and independence scores are about equal; group is slightly ahead on comparison (9 against 8 against 6).
- No frozen falsifier fired. Detail: group trails none in financing by 0.25 question per reader, under the 1-question threshold. The
  wrong-group questions scored the same in every view.

**Traces read.**
- C3: group readers saw both Lisa Su accounts, but read the ambiguous sentence as covering MI450 only. That is a judgement point, not a
  missed detail.
- R5: group readers put "orders" and "sales" side by side, while none readers added an inferred year.
- F1 is partial everywhere because grading was strict.

**Council B** (`council/group/c-*`).
- The test supports preserving later text. It does not prove equivalence with no merging, overall dossier quality (the questions were
  chosen for added details), or wrong-group safety (the questions pointed readers at the facts).
- Size is about no merging, up to 25% more in competition: groups bring members whose own links point elsewhere. Grouping gives
  structure, not compression.
- Next class: wrong groups.

**Wrong-group census ($0; the 9 no-home merges, read against exactly what Jev saw):**
- M2, Sharon AI into Firmus: the incoming record's quote is the whole paragraph, Firmus sentence included, so Jev matched on the quote.
  Step 1 bundle on the incoming side.
- M57, NVL576 into NVL144: the stored record's own summary also states the NVL576 claim, so the merge is defensible. Step 1 bundle on
  the stored side.
- M30, analysts' 82% and 41% into the analysts' revenue path: different figures. A Jev error.
- 6 arguable (the same announcement, the same figure, or a relayed report): under grouping both texts sit side by side.
- So 2 real wrong groups out of 102, and their texts survive.

**Open for Alex:**
- the several-match rule (pending, best match, or own entry with references);
- the Step 2 pass lines.

## 11. Log rows

| Arm | Hypothesis | Change | Result | Kept |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Grouping (A) | Keeping each repeat's text keeps added details noticeable without double counting | Isolated library and group view | Detail 25/36, the same as no merging, against 3/36 source-only; 0 double counting; size about the same as no merging | yes (Alex's decision; tested) |

## 12. Close-out (2026-11-08)

**Alex's decisions (2026-11-08):**
- a record that is a repeat of several groups joins only the one Jev judges it most like (the highest same_statement probability; ties
  go to the earliest group);
- the Step 2 lines: (1) search at least 90%; (2) clear wrong merges at most 2%; (3) grouped dossiers keep no fewer later details than
  no merging.

Both are recorded in PRD §5.

**Built.**
- `clean-arch/step2/compare.py`: search, Jev comparison, the outcome with best match, forward order, and a failed comparison refused and
  reported. `test_compare.py`: 6 tests; all 4 mutants caught.
- `run_forward.py` reads a stored Step 1 trace directly.
- **Run** (`poc/data/clean-step2-forward-2026-11-08/`, a fresh Jev draw): 282 records made 178 groups.
  - 104 repeats, 3 revisions, 0 refused; 16 records had several same_statement answers.
  - The cached embedding texts were verified identical: 282 of 282 documents, 313 of 313 queries.

**Council A** (`council/group/d-*`):
- report search as recall over known labelled counterparts;
- blind-review every merge, previously labelled positives included;
- verify the cache texts;
- re-run the reader test on the new views.

| Line | Result | Met |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Search | 112/113 known labelled counterparts had a holding group among the candidates (99.1%). For 107 of them the group's original, which is what Jev saw, is itself a counterpart. This is not recall over all real repeats. | yes |
| 2. Clear wrong merges | 104 merges read by two blind readers; 85 accepted by both; the 19 rejected by either went to a third reader: acceptable 1, overlap 15, **wrong 3** = 2.9% | **no** (missed by one merge) |
| 3. Later details | Reader test re-run on the rebuilt views with the frozen questions and key: detail none 27.5, source 3, group **28** of 36; unsupported claims 3 / 2 / 2; double counting 0 | yes |

**Line 2 detail.**
- The 3 wrong merges:
  - NVL576 into the NVL144 group, twice. The group's original Step 1 record states both claims.
  - Analysts' 82% and 41% growth into the analysts' revenue-path record: different figures, a Jev error.
- 15 overlaps, which the third reader called imperfect but not misleading to a reader of the record's own text. Among them:
  - orders against sales ($1tn);
  - expected revenue against committed off-take (Firmus);
  - bundled records: the business model into the Sharon group, the Kyber delay report into the backup-rack group, the Taiwan raid
    alongside the Singapore mansion.
- My own reading had 5 wrong (Sharon AI into Firmus, and the business-model bundle into the Sharon group, both overlap to the third
  reader). Both readings miss the line.

**Council B** (`council/group/e-*`):
- do not offer the result as a pass;
- report 3 wrong, 15 overlap and 1 acceptable after dispute;
- a later look at bundled records would explain only part of it;
- stop and report.

**Verdict.** Step 2 meets lines 1 and 3 and misses line 2 by one merge, in one Jev draw. Per Alex's instruction, the work stops here,
and the census goes to him.

**Not done:** the unprompted wrong-group reading test, and a fix for line 2.

## 32. Step 2 re-measured on the c4 records; Jev's criteria aligned with the merge line (2026-11-08)

**Run** (`clean-step2-forward-c4-2026-11-08/`): 289 records made 179 groups; 110 repeats, 4 revisions, 0 refused.

**Line 1, search** (the reference carried onto the new records by `map_reference.py`: an identity rule on shared verbatim passages in the
same article; 89% of the old records map, 326 of 333 same-statement pairs): **104 of 105 known counterparts found (99.0%), met.**

**Line 2, wrong merges** (two blind Codex readers per packet, a third on every pair either rejected; the same prompts as before, packets
built by `build_merge_packets.py`): **8 of 110 wrong (7.3%), missed**, against 3 of 104 before. Each wrong merge read:
- **6 are one cascade.** Step 1 put SemiAnalysis's Kyber-delay report and NVIDIA's denial ("Our roadmap is intact") into one record
  (49:e1). Every later outlet's denial was then judged by Jev a "same_statement" of that record, with probability 0.79–0.96.
  - In k6b d1, k6b d2 and c2 the denial was its own record. Five re-sends of article 49 with c4 (`probe-r8-kyber-c4/`) separated it
    5/5. So the bundling is rare (1 of 9 samples), but one bundle of a widely repeated statement multiplies into many wrong merges.
  - The earlier Step 2 run's wrong merges were the same class (NVL576 into the NVL144 record, twice).
- **The other 2 are Jev errors at low confidence:**
  - X30, the analysts' $253bn → $392bn path against 82%/41% growth, the same pair as the earlier run (0.52);
  - X99, China data-centre revenue at zero against no H200 revenue (0.57).
- **A probability cut is not a fix.** Below 0.6, the c4 run's merges are 3 wrong and 4 acceptable; the earlier run's are 0 wrong and 5
  acceptable.
- **An original-party identity rule is not a fix either.** The free-text party differs in 28 accepted merges ("Firmus Technologies" and
  "Firmus").

**One-ruler fix (AGENTS §7.1).**
- **The mismatch:** the merge line's test is "later reports earlier's **main** statement"; production's Jev criterion was "the same
  evidence".
- **The fix:** the clean Step 2 now asks Jev its own piece question:
  - same_statement = the incoming piece reports the stored piece's main statement; a report of only a secondary statement is not it;
  - supersedes keeps "an official confirms or denies that reported claim".
- **The replay** (`…-p2/`; every other cached answer reused): 108 repeats, 3 revisions.
  - Verdicts were carried to the 95 identical pairs; the 13 new pairs were read by two readers and one disputed pair by the third.
  - **4 of 108 wrong (3.7%).**
  - X30 and X99 no longer merge. Two denials became a revision of the report and a repeat of the standalone denial group.
  - **The 4 left are the early denials into the bundled record 49:e1**, which arrived before any standalone denial group existed.
- **Every other merge is acceptable or overlap.**

**Later linking on the new criteria:** 173 judged, 1 linked (Valar). Line 3 (the reader test) was not re-measured: its dossiers are
keyed to the old run's thesis ids.

**Next (the root of the remaining class).**
- Step 1's unit, from the signed standard's own definition, "陈述：原文里某一方说的一句话或一件事" (a statement is what one party said):
  one item holds one party's statement, and another party's response to it is its own item.
- The c4 sentence "an estimate and a target price … drawn from it are two statements" is the same rule and is folded into it.

## 33. Arm c5: one party's statement per item (2026-11-08)

**c5** = c4 plus one closing-check sentence before "Return only the evidence items you keep":
- the sentence: "Each item you keep holds one party's statement: another party's response to it (a denial, a confirmation, a comment) is
  its own item, and so is a valuation someone draws from an estimate";
- c4's system sentence "An estimate and a target price or valuation someone draws from it are two statements" is removed, because the
  general rule now carries it;
- sources: the signed standard's glossary, "陈述：原文里某一方说的一句话或一件事"; K6b §4, "one evidence item records one statement";
  Alex's EPS/target ruling;
- size: system 14,491 → 14,403; closing 8,114 → 8,302.

**Check sends, 2 draws each** (`probe-r9-c5/`, $0.14):

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Kyber article 49 | the denial is its own item 2/2 |
| d1-57, d1-62 | one speaker's revenue and margin guidance stays one item; no over-splitting (3 and 7–8 items, as under c4) |
| d1-66 | EPS kept, target dropped |
| pos-1 | credit-support thesis opened |

**Runs launched in parallel**, inputs byte-identical (source sha256 checked):
- `gold-c5-flash/` (115 dev);
- `test-c5-flash/` (26 test, scored once for c5).

The runner retries a cut answer (§30). Step 2 follows on the c5 dev records with the aligned Jev criteria (§32).

## 34. c5 measured; Step 2 lines 1–2 met on its records; c6 narrows the rule and raises the output cap (2026-11-08)

**c5 test** (`test-c5-flash/`, once): helpful **38/42**, core 9/9, **noise 11** (c4 4), items 57, theses 9 (0 small, 0 duplicates).

**c5 dev** (`gold-c5-flash/`): 114 of 115. Article 54 (`…9756d6`, the SemiAnalysis backstop article, 16 helpful entries) was cut at the
32k output cap twice and failed; the run continued, as Alex's rule says.

| On the 114 articles both completed | **c5** | c4 |
|---|---|---|
| Helpful (of 218) | 204 | 203 |
| Core | 80 | 79 |
| Not-kept spans kept | **39** | 33 |

**Regression read item by item on dev** (tuning set):
- **What:** the extra noise is other parties' remarks extracted as their own items (Mizuho's and Bloomberg's analysts' remarks, a
  defendant's lawyers' statement, Huang's "parabolic", startup CEOs' IPO plans).
- **Mechanism:** c5's "another party's response to it (a denial, a confirmation, **a comment**) is its own item" licensed creating items
  from remarks, not only unfolding a bundle.
- The test showed the same direction.

**The output cap is too low for the longest articles.**
- Article 54 took 27k completion tokens in c2, 18k in c4, and over 32k twice in c5.
- Re-sent once with a 64k cap, it completed: 37,210 tokens (32,074 reasoning), valid JSON, 16 items.
- The cap was an implementation detail of the close-out (32,000), not a setting Alex chose. **Raised to 64,000.** Only long answers use
  more.

**Step 2 on the c5 records** (`clean-step2-forward-c5-2026-11-08/`, aligned Jev criteria):
- **Kyber split cleanly:** the report group with 10 retellings, the denial group with 6.
- Line 1, search: **94 of 96 (97.9%), met.** The reference is now mapped by input id: c5's failed article 54 had shifted the numbering
  of every later article, so 34% mapped before the fix and 86% after; c4's mapping is unchanged at 89%.
- Line 2, wrong merges: **2 of 105 (1.9%), met.** Both are isolated Jev errors: two different revenue-sharing programmes (0.84); three
  companies' water work against NVIDIA's DSX design (0.50).
- Later linking: 325 judged, 4 linked.

**Identity fix in Step 2:** `run_forward.step1_records` and `build_merge_packets` number an article by its position in the first
segment's manifest, so a failed item no longer shifts later ids (AGENTS §3, identity). c4 and c2 numbers are unchanged; stored c5 Step
2 results stay internally consistent.

**c6** = c5 with:
- the closing sentence narrowed to "Do not fold another party's statement into an item: a report and the denial or confirmation of it are
  two items, and so are an estimate and a valuation someone draws from it, each kept only if it passes the test above";
- max_output_tokens 64,000.

**Checks** (`probe-r10-c6/`, 2 draws each, $0.14):
- Kyber denial separate 2/2; no over-splitting (d1-57);
- the lawyers' statement and the Mizuho and Bloomberg remarks are gone;
- startup CEOs' own IPO remarks remain (their own statements, not folds).

`gold-c6-flash/` and `test-c6-flash/` launched 04:10, inputs byte-identical.

## 35. c6 measured: Step 2 lines 1–2 met; Step 1 misses only "no fragments" by one per set; the question gold is far stricter than the readers (2026-11-08)

**c6 dev** (`gold-c6-flash/`): 115 of 115 in 115 calls; articles 54 and 59 completed under the 64k cap with no retries.

**c6 test** (`test-c6-flash/`, once):

- misses: the valuation assumptions (Alex's ruling) and the telecom providers working on AI-RAN.

**Step 2 on the c6 records** (`clean-step2-forward-c6-2026-11-08/`):
- 291 records → 187 groups, 104 repeats; Kyber split cleanly (report 10, denial 8);
- line 1, search: **95 of 97 (97.9%), met**;
- line 2, wrong merges: **2 of 104 (1.9%), met** (X4, the two revenue-sharing programmes, recurring; X83);
- later linking: 242 judged, 3 linked;
- line 3 not re-measured (dossiers keyed to the old thesis ids; Step 3's grouping code unchanged since it passed).

**The two duplicates, traced.**
- **The theses:** dev "AI labs building their own custom inference chips (DeepSeek, OpenAI)" against the open "non-Huawei competitors or
  alternative stacks such as Cerebras"; test "xAI's Colossus 2 buildout" against the open "neocloud GPU rental prices as the demand
  read-out".
- **The model's accounts** (`gold-c6-flash/fragment-accounts.json`): it applied K6b's separate-bet test ("their answers can move apart")
  with analyst reasons: customer insourcing is not merchant competition; one lab's deployment is not neocloud pricing.
- **The frozen question gold** marks both must_not: "A DeepSeek chip development question" and "An OpenAI Jalapeno deployment question";
  "Will xAI's Colossus 2 reach about 1.21 million NVIDIA GPUs by the end of 2026?". So they are errors by both references, not a
  reader's threshold.

**Census: theses against the frozen question gold** (c6 dev 20, test 10; read against each opening article's must_not):

  - the Singapore case;
  - AI debt above $7T;

- **The required openings are present:** credit support, Kyber NVL144, China access, supply commitments.
- **Most of the must_not theses were judged "bet" by the readers.** k6b and c4 opened theses of the same kinds (c4's test opened the same
  xAI thesis, then not flagged because nothing overlapped).
- **So:** the reader-based pass line (small ≤ 3, fragments 0) and the frozen question gold disagree widely on what merits its own
  thesis. Which one governs Step 1's thesis granularity is Alex's call (the council-loop trap: when references split on "how big is
  big", his rulings are the ruler).

**Status against the agreed lines** (one draw each):

12	# Review of Jev usage and reranker positioning
13	
14	Reviewed on **2026-10-25**. This review covers the requested parts of sections 3–6. It does not redesign extraction, change the pipeline, or authorize a paid experiment.
15	
16	I read public vendor documentation, repository sources, stored evaluation answers, and relevant papers. I made no paid model calls. Calculations below use saved answers; they are not new model measurements.
17	
18	## 1. Latest TypeSafe API
19	
20	### Versions and changes
21	
22	TypeSafe identifies **`jev-1.14.0`**, released October 14, as its newest model. **`jev-1.13.0` remains supported**. Both `jev-latest` and `jev-preview` currently resolve to 1.14.0. A version pin matters because changing an alias can change answers under an existing threshold. [Models](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models)
23	
24	The release announcement describes incremental improvements, with the largest expected gain in multilingual support. It also introduces experimental image input, a `box` answer type, and longer context. Images are enabled for both versions; `box` is restricted to 1.14.0. These experimental features are explicitly less mature than ordinary text decisions. The announcement does **not** establish a quantified improvement on Chinese grouping or identity. [Jev 1.14 announcement](https://typesafe.ai/blog/jev-1-14)
25	
26	### Request and response shapes
27	
28	The endpoint remains **`POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone`**, using bearer authentication. The required body fields are `model`, `state`, and `questions`. `questions` is an object keyed by caller-chosen identifiers. The response contains `model`, `answers` under those identifiers, and token `usage`. [API reference](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api/system-one)
29	
30	`state` accepts a string, object, or array. The old repository’s requirement that it be a nonempty string is a narrower local contract. [State documentation](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/state), [Old client:28–29](/Users/lchingen/tn-hivemind/src/tn_hivemind/models/jev.py:28)
31	
32	| Type | Question shape | Answer shape and meaning |
33	|---|---|---|
34	| `choice` | `instructions`; `criteria` object mapping labels to descriptions | `type`, winning `choice`, per-label `probabilities`, `confidence`. Appropriate for unordered categories. [Choice](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/choice) |
35	| `score` | `instructions`; ordered `criteria` array | `type`, numerical `score`, `legend`, per-level `probabilities`, `confidence`. The score is the expected level index, from zero to the highest index. [Score](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/score) |
36	| `noul` | Yes/no instructions; optional criteria explaining true/false | `type` and `noul`, the probability of yes. It does **not** return a separate confidence field. [Noul](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/noul) |
37	| `box` | Experimental image-location question | Bounding-box coordinates; requires the image opt-in header. Irrelevant to this text POC. [API schema](https://api.typesafe.ai/openapi.json) |
38	
39	Instructions and descriptions can use structured values; strings are sufficient here. The question identifier itself is not model context, so a target named only `g1` would be insufficient. Claude’s example includes the target description in `instructions`, which avoids that problem. [Structured instructions](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/advanced), [Choice](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/choice)
40	
41	### Limits and prices
42	
43	| Item | Current documented value |
44	|---|---|
45	| Input price, both versions | **$0.042 per million input tokens**; output tokens free. [Models](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models) |
46	| Questions per request | No separate numerical cap; context limits apply. [Models](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models) |
47	| Default request context | **64k tokens:** state plus all questions. [Models](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models) |
48	| Default per-question context | **32k tokens:** state plus one question. [Models](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models) |
49	| Experimental long context | Both limits become **262k** with `TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Long-Context: true`; documented as slower and less accurate. [Models](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models) |

53	| Score criteria | Maximum **10**. OpenAPI permits one; prose documentation says the scale should have at least two. [OpenAPI](https://api.typesafe.ai/openapi.json), [Score](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/score) |

83	### Probability, confidence, and calibration
84	
85	TypeSafe markets Jev as trained for calibrated decisions using RLCD. That is a vendor claim about training, not proof of calibration on this repository’s labels. [TypeSafe’s description](https://typesafe.ai/)
86	
87	For a Choice with \(n\) options, the current documented formula is:
88	
89	\[
90	\mathrm{confidence}
91	=\frac{p_{\max}-1/n}{1-1/n}.
92	\]
93	
94	Thus, for three options, confidence **0.95** corresponds to a winning probability of approximately **0.9667**, not 0.95. A winning probability of 0.90 corresponds to confidence 0.85. A confident `cannot_tell` is still `cannot_tell`. [Confidence](https://docs.typesafe.ai/confidence)
95	
96	The plan must name which field it thresholds. The old tagging policy thresholds **`confidence`**. Choosing that threshold on dev does not, by itself, demonstrate that probability bins match empirical success rates. [Tagging policy:595–618](/Users/lchingen/tn-hivemind/src/tn_hivemind/data/relations.py:595)
97	
98	The old wrapper records two-decimal rounding as an **observed behavior** and allows resulting summation error. I found no basis for promoting that observation into a permanent precision guarantee. [Old validator:79–94](/Users/lchingen/tn-hivemind/src/tn_hivemind/models/jev.py:79), [Current schema](https://api.typesafe.ai/openapi.json)
99	
100	### Batching, latency, retention, and SDKs
101	
102	**Batching is supported and encouraged.** TypeSafe says each question is evaluated separately against the shared state. Its fan-out pattern explicitly places several questions in one request. This supports one candidate and quote in shared state, with one target-specific question per recalled card. It is not a listwise comparison among all targets. [Fan-out](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/fan-out)
103	
104	The vendor’s older Jev 1.12 cookbook compares 13 batched questions with 13 sequential requests over a 53,777-character document. It reports **0.27 seconds versus 2.71 seconds**, and **$0.000497 versus $0.006090**. These are workload-specific results against sequential calls, not a universal latency promise. Several answers exhibit small run-to-run variation, contradicting an assumption of guaranteed exact repeatability. [Parallel-question experiment](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/parallel_questions)
105	
106	The **70–500 ms** figure is a vendor launch claim, not a measured latency for this POC or its largest batches. [Launch announcement](https://typesafe.ai/blog/introducing-system-one-models-and-jev)
107	
108	TypeSafe says it does not train on customer requests or responses. **Zero data retention is an enterprise offering, not the documented default.** The public privacy policy and DPA use necessity-based retention language rather than a fixed universal deletion period. [Legal overview](https://docs.typesafe.ai/legal), [Privacy policy](https://typesafe.ai/legal/privacy-policy), [DPA](https://typesafe.ai/legal/data-processing)
109	
110	Official clients include Python **`typesafe-sdk`**, with synchronous and asynchronous clients, and JavaScript/TypeScript **`@typesafe-ai/sdk`**. The JavaScript documentation specifies Node.js 22+. [Python SDK](https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/python), [JavaScript SDK](https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/javascript)
111	
112	**Access limits of this review:** the public documentation, OpenAPI, cookbooks, release announcement, and legal text were readable without login. I did not access the account console, authenticate to the API, verify the account balance, or measure current service latency. Current numerical account rate limits and current payment status remain unverified.
113	
114	### Direct vendor examples relevant to this review
115	
116	- **Reranking:** a Jev 1.12 cookbook retrieves 30 legal candidates with BM25 and judges query–candidate pairs using Noul. Across 40 queries, it reports rounded top-1 retrieval success rising from **5% to 18%**, top-5 from **15% to 35%**, and top-10 from **38% to 62%**. This supports the intended pattern, not a grouping accuracy forecast. [Reranking cookbook](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/rerank_typesafe)
117	- **Entity matching:** another Jev 1.12 example processes **450 preblocked beer pairs**, using a three-level Score plus field-specific Nouls. It produces **40 same-entity assertions, 50 review cases, and 360 unlinked pairs**. Those are routing counts; the page does not report accuracy against gold labels. [Entity-alignment cookbook](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/entity_alignment)

119	## 2. What the old repository actually did
120	
121	### Two different cascades
122	
123	The plan combines two distinct uses.
124	
125	**Relationship tagging:** `tag_state` supplies the subject, counterparty, first quote, and additional quotes as context. One request asks three Choice questions:
126	
127	1. The counterparty’s role relative to the subject.
128	2. What flows between them, or the market in which they compete.
129	3. The subject’s stated dependence on the counterparty.
130	
131	The instructions require grounding in the quote. [relations.py:543–577](/Users/lchingen/tn-hivemind/src/tn_hivemind/data/relations.py:543)
132	
133	The selected cascade keeps extraction’s labels unless Jev confidently disagrees on **role or channel**, which triggers an isolated Luna adjudication. Dependency disagreement does not trigger this policy, and direct Jev dependency replacement is disabled by `jev_dependency: False`. [relations.py:588–619](/Users/lchingen/tn-hivemind/src/tn_hivemind/data/relations.py:588)
134	
135	**Evidence relations:** the historical implementation asks whether evidence `supports`, `contradicts`, is `contextual` to, or is `irrelevant` to a premise. Its cascade **accepts Jev’s answer directly at confidence ≥0.95**, otherwise asking Luna. Here Jev is a first-pass decider, not merely a disagreement check.
136	
137	Historical source: `/Users/lchingen/tn-hivemind/src/tn_hivemind/edges_v4.py:65–117`, read at commit `79540ee74b3f5c210ebb9a11bee8fad180fbedf1`. The current decision record also describes this optional Jev-first evidence cascade. [Old DECISIONS.md:968](/Users/lchingen/tn-hivemind/docs/DECISIONS.md:968)

139	That historical file judges each premise–evidence pair in isolation because earlier shared context allowed reasons to borrow neighboring facts. This is an isolation requirement for the material presented to a judgment; it does not establish that TypeSafe requires one question per HTTP request. Historical source: the same `edges_v4.py:1–7`.

Its difficult cases include mismatched periods, segment versus total scope, forecasts versus actuals, and different entities. The gold is explicitly **cross-family model-authored, not human gold**. 314	## 4. Literature on the positioning
315	
316	### Is retrieval followed by a closed-set pair classifier recognized?
317	
318	**Yes.** Dense or lexical retrieval can produce a shortlist, after which a model reads both sides and estimates a task-specific relation. Sentence Transformers documents retrieval followed by cross-encoder relevance scoring. Entity matching commonly calls candidate reduction **blocking**, then applies pair classification; Ditto is a clear example. [Retrieve and rerank](https://sbert.net/examples/sentence_transformer/applications/retrieve_rerank/README.html), [Ditto](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.00584)
319	
320	A classifier and a reranker are not mutually exclusive categories. Sorting candidate pairs by the probability of the desired class makes the classifier act as a reranker. Applying a threshold then adds an acceptance decision. Probability-based ranking has a substantial literature, including explicit analysis of calibration and uncertainty. [Penha and Hauff](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.04356)
321	
322	There is also a close grouping precedent: Saravanakumar et al. combine document–cluster similarity with a neural decision about joining an existing cluster or creating another. Their representation is not the exact Jev card-pair design, so this supports the general pattern rather than validating this implementation. [Event-driven news clustering](https://aclanthology.org/2021.eacl-main.198.pdf)
323	
324	### What performance ranges have been reported?
325	
326	These metrics are deliberately kept separate. **Accuracy, pairwise F1, and clustering F1 are not interchangeable.**
327	
328	| Task | Published result | Relevance and limitation |
329	|---|---|---|
330	| Duplicate-question detection, QQP | BERT-base **71.2 F1**, BERT-large **72.1 F1** on the official GLUE test evaluation | Task-trained pair classifiers; Table 1 explicitly reports F1 for QQP. These are not Jev forecasts. [BERT, Table 1](https://aclanthology.org/N19-1423.pdf) |
331	| Entity matching | Ditto: **75.58 F1** on Amazon–Google, **94.37** on Beer, **98.99** on DBLP–ACM, **100.00** on Fodors–Zagats | Wide dataset variation despite the same general method. These are trained matching systems, not generic relevance scores. [Ditto, Table 5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.00584) |
332	| News-event clustering | Compared systems span **89.76–94.76 B-cubed F1**; the authors’ full system reaches **94.76** | Their dense-only variant reaches **68.98**, demonstrating that representation and task definition matter. These are event clusters, not overlapping thesis memberships. [News clustering, Table 1](https://aclanthology.org/2021.eacl-main.198.pdf) |
333	
334	The literature supports **testing the pattern**. It does not support an expected accuracy number for this repository without its own accepted labels and evaluation.
335	
336	### Known failure modes
337	
338	- **Part-of versus same.** Event-coreference research explicitly distinguishes full identity from subevent relations. That supports keeping containment separate instead of treating it as weaker identity. [Araki et al.](https://aclanthology.org/L14-1725/)
339	- **Temporal differences.** The news-clustering paper reports incorrect merges without temporal information. In entity linking, source dates can exclude otherwise plausible namesakes. [News clustering](https://aclanthology.org/2021.eacl-main.198.pdf), [Historical entity linking](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10462-024-11102-9)
340	- **Popularity bias.** Historical entity-linking experiments measure systems preferring more popular entities over less common correct ones. This is evidence of a general risk, not a measured Jev defect on company stories. [Graciotti et al., Table 10](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10462-024-11102-9)
341	- **Similar wording with different identity.** Ditto’s examples include nearly identical product descriptions whose edition or grade changes the correct answer, and differently worded descriptions that identify the same product. [Ditto](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.00584)
342	- **Uncalibrated confidence.** Neural rankers can rank usefully while their numerical scores remain unreliable as probabilities. Conversely, calibration does not repair an incorrectly defined label. [Ranker calibration](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.04356), [Classifier calibration](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v70/guo17a.html)
343	- **Jev-specific boundaries.** TypeSafe’s 1.13 guidance warns about numerical/date reasoning, indirection, distracting context, and option-order effects. These support keeping explicit numerical conflicts in code and measuring semantic judgments on the actual task. They are not quantified 1.14 failure rates. [Jev 1.13 limitations](https://docs.typesafe.ai/model-jaggedness/jev-1.13)
344	
345	### Choice, Score, or one question per call?
346	
347	For the plan’s unordered relation labels, **Choice is the appropriate starting type**. A binary membership question could use Noul; retaining an explicit insufficient-information category makes Choice reasonable. Score is appropriate only when the owner-defined property is genuinely ordered. The vendor’s entity example shows Score is possible, not mandatory. [Choice](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/choice), [Score](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/score), [Entity example](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/entity_alignment)
348	
349	Neither the API nor the old repository establishes a general requirement for one question per call. The old tagger already batches three. The important distinction is **one clearly defined judgment per question**, with the facts that judgment needs—not one HTTP request per judgment. [Old tagger:568–577](/Users/lchingen/tn-hivemind/src/tn_hivemind/data/relations.py:568), [Fan-out](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/fan-out)

[Plan:30,62,78](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-10-25-retrieval-poc/rerank-grouping-plan.md:62), [Old results](/Users/lchingen/tn-hivemind/docs/BENCHMARK.md:190)

[Old policy:595–618](/Users/lchingen/tn-hivemind/src/tn_hivemind/data/relations.py:595), [Threshold guidance](https://docs.typesafe.ai/confidence)

# Review of Jev usage and reranker positioning

Reviewed on **2026-10-25**. This review covers the requested parts of sections 3–6. It does not redesign extraction, change the pipeline, or authorize a paid experiment.

I read public vendor documentation, repository sources, stored evaluation answers, and relevant papers. I made no paid model calls. Calculations below use saved answers; they are not new model measurements.

## 1. Latest TypeSafe API

### Versions and changes

TypeSafe identifies **`jev-1.14.0`**, released October 14, as its newest model. **`jev-1.13.0` remains supported**. Both `jev-latest` and `jev-preview` currently resolve to 1.14.0. A version pin matters because changing an alias can change answers under an existing threshold. [Models](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models)

The release announcement describes incremental improvements, with the largest expected gain in multilingual support. It also introduces experimental image input, a `box` answer type, and longer context. Images are enabled for both versions; `box` is restricted to 1.14.0. These experimental features are explicitly less mature than ordinary text decisions. The announcement does **not** establish a quantified improvement on Chinese grouping or identity. [Jev 1.14 announcement](https://typesafe.ai/blog/jev-1-14)

### Request and response shapes

The endpoint remains **`POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone`**, using bearer authentication. The required body fields are `model`, `state`, and `questions`. `questions` is an object keyed by caller-chosen identifiers. The response contains `model`, `answers` under those identifiers, and token `usage`. [API reference](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api/system-one)

`state` accepts a string, object, or array. The old repository’s requirement that it be a nonempty string is a narrower local contract. [State documentation](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/state), [Old client:28–29](/Users/lchingen/tn-hivemind/src/tn_hivemind/models/jev.py:28)

| Type | Question shape | Answer shape and meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `choice` | `instructions`; `criteria` object mapping labels to descriptions | `type`, winning `choice`, per-label `probabilities`, `confidence`. Appropriate for unordered categories. [Choice](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/choice) |
| `score` | `instructions`; ordered `criteria` array | `type`, numerical `score`, `legend`, per-level `probabilities`, `confidence`. The score is the expected level index, from zero to the highest index. [Score](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/score) |
| `noul` | Yes/no instructions; optional criteria explaining true/false | `type` and `noul`, the probability of yes. It does **not** return a separate confidence field. [Noul](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/noul) |
| `box` | Experimental image-location question | Bounding-box coordinates; requires the image opt-in header. Irrelevant to this text POC. [API schema](https://api.typesafe.ai/openapi.json) |

Instructions and descriptions can use structured values; strings are sufficient here. The question identifier itself is not model context, so a target named only `g1` would be insufficient. Claude’s example includes the target description in `instructions`, which avoids that problem. [Structured instructions](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/advanced), [Choice](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/choice)

### Limits and prices

| Item | Current documented value |
|---|---|
| Input price, both versions | **$0.042 per million input tokens**; output tokens free. [Models](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models) |
| Questions per request | No separate numerical cap; context limits apply. [Models](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models) |
| Default request context | **64k tokens:** state plus all questions. [Models](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models) |
| Default per-question context | **32k tokens:** state plus one question. [Models](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models) |
| Experimental long context | Both limits become **262k** with `TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Long-Context: true`; documented as slower and less accurate. [Models](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models) |
| HTTP body | **32 MiB**, independently of token limits. [Request rules](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api/errors) |
| Encoding and nesting | UTF-8 JSON without BOM; maximum 64 nested levels; finite numbers. [Request rules](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api/errors) |
| Choice criteria | Maximum **255**. The OpenAPI schema allows a minimum of one; a meaningful comparison normally needs alternatives. [OpenAPI](https://api.typesafe.ai/openapi.json) |
| Score criteria | Maximum **10**. OpenAPI permits one; prose documentation says the scale should have at least two. [OpenAPI](https://api.typesafe.ai/openapi.json), [Score](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/score) |

### Minimal correct request

This adapts the documented support-ticket example. It is illustrative; I did not send it.

```json
{
  "model": "jev-1.14.0",
  "state": "The customer says their subscription was charged twice.",
  "questions": {
    "issue": {
      "type": "choice",
      "instructions": "Which issue does the message report?",
      "criteria": {
        "duplicate_charge": "The same fee was charged more than once.",
        "other": "A different issue is reported."
      }

```

Send this JSON to the endpoint above with the bearer and JSON content-type headers. Read the result at `answers.issue`; do not expect generated explanation text. [API request examples](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api/system-one)

### Probability, confidence, and calibration

TypeSafe markets Jev as trained for calibrated decisions using RLCD. That is a vendor claim about training, not proof of calibration on this repository’s labels. [TypeSafe’s description](https://typesafe.ai/)

For a Choice with \(n\) options, the current documented formula is:

\[
\mathrm{confidence}
=\frac{p_{\max}-1/n}{1-1/n}.
\]

Thus, for three options, confidence **0.95** corresponds to a winning probability of approximately **0.9667**, not 0.95. A winning probability of 0.90 corresponds to confidence 0.85. A confident `cannot_tell` is still `cannot_tell`. [Confidence](https://docs.typesafe.ai/confidence)

The plan must name which field it thresholds. The old tagging policy thresholds **`confidence`**. Choosing that threshold on dev does not, by itself, demonstrate that probability bins match empirical success rates. [Tagging policy:595–618](/Users/lchingen/tn-hivemind/src/tn_hivemind/data/relations.py:595)

The old wrapper records two-decimal rounding as an **observed behavior** and allows resulting summation error. I found no basis for promoting that observation into a permanent precision guarantee. [Old validator:79–94](/Users/lchingen/tn-hivemind/src/tn_hivemind/models/jev.py:79), [Current schema](https://api.typesafe.ai/openapi.json)

### Batching, latency, retention, and SDKs

**Batching is supported and encouraged.** TypeSafe says each question is evaluated separately against the shared state. Its fan-out pattern explicitly places several questions in one request. This supports one candidate and quote in shared state, with one target-specific question per recalled card. It is not a listwise comparison among all targets. [Fan-out](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/fan-out)

The vendor’s older Jev 1.12 cookbook compares 13 batched questions with 13 sequential requests over a 53,777-character document. It reports **0.27 seconds versus 2.71 seconds**, and **$0.000497 versus $0.006090**. These are workload-specific results against sequential calls, not a universal latency promise. Several answers exhibit small run-to-run variation, contradicting an assumption of guaranteed exact repeatability. [Parallel-question experiment](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/parallel_questions)

The **70–500 ms** figure is a vendor launch claim, not a measured latency for this POC or its largest batches. [Launch announcement](https://typesafe.ai/blog/introducing-system-one-models-and-jev)

TypeSafe says it does not train on customer requests or responses. **Zero data retention is an enterprise offering, not the documented default.** The public privacy policy and DPA use necessity-based retention language rather than a fixed universal deletion period. [Legal overview](https://docs.typesafe.ai/legal), [Privacy policy](https://typesafe.ai/legal/privacy-policy), [DPA](https://typesafe.ai/legal/data-processing)

Official clients include Python **`typesafe-sdk`**, with synchronous and asynchronous clients, and JavaScript/TypeScript **`@typesafe-ai/sdk`**. The JavaScript documentation specifies Node.js 22+. [Python SDK](https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/python), [JavaScript SDK](https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/javascript)

**Access limits of this review:** the public documentation, OpenAPI, cookbooks, release announcement, and legal text were readable without login. I did not access the account console, authenticate to the API, verify the account balance, or measure current service latency. Current numerical account rate limits and current payment status remain unverified.

### Direct vendor examples relevant to this review

- **Reranking:** a Jev 1.12 cookbook retrieves 30 legal candidates with BM25 and judges query–candidate pairs using Noul. Across 40 queries, it reports rounded top-1 retrieval success rising from **5% to 18%**, top-5 from **15% to 35%**, and top-10 from **38% to 62%**. This supports the intended pattern, not a grouping accuracy forecast. [Reranking cookbook](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/rerank_typesafe)
- **Entity matching:** another Jev 1.12 example processes **450 preblocked beer pairs**, using a three-level Score plus field-specific Nouls. It produces **40 same-entity assertions, 50 review cases, and 360 unlinked pairs**. Those are routing counts; the page does not report accuracy against gold labels. [Entity-alignment cookbook](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/entity_alignment)

## 2. What the old repository actually did

### Two different cascades

The plan combines two distinct uses.

**Relationship tagging:** `tag_state` supplies the subject, counterparty, first quote, and additional quotes as context. One request asks three Choice questions:

1. The counterparty’s role relative to the subject.
2. What flows between them, or the market in which they compete.
3. The subject’s stated dependence on the counterparty.

The instructions require grounding in the quote. [relations.py:543–577](/Users/lchingen/tn-hivemind/src/tn_hivemind/data/relations.py:543)

The selected cascade keeps extraction’s labels unless Jev confidently disagrees on **role or channel**, which triggers an isolated Luna adjudication. Dependency disagreement does not trigger this policy, and direct Jev dependency replacement is disabled by `jev_dependency: False`. [relations.py:588–619](/Users/lchingen/tn-hivemind/src/tn_hivemind/data/relations.py:588)

**Evidence relations:** the historical implementation asks whether evidence `supports`, `contradicts`, is `contextual` to, or is `irrelevant` to a premise. Its cascade **accepts Jev’s answer directly at confidence ≥0.95**, otherwise asking Luna. Here Jev is a first-pass decider, not merely a disagreement check.

Historical source: `/Users/lchingen/tn-hivemind/src/tn_hivemind/edges_v4.py:65–117`, read at commit `79540ee74b3f5c210ebb9a11bee8fad180fbedf1`. The current decision record also describes this optional Jev-first evidence cascade. [Old DECISIONS.md:968](/Users/lchingen/tn-hivemind/docs/DECISIONS.md:968)

That historical file judges each premise–evidence pair in isolation because earlier shared context allowed reasons to borrow neighboring facts. This is an isolation requirement for the material presented to a judgment; it does not establish that TypeSafe requires one question per HTTP request. Historical source: the same `edges_v4.py:1–7`.

[Plan:70](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-10-25-retrieval-poc/rerank-grouping-plan.md:70), [Ditto’s contrasting high- and low-overlap examples](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.00584)

The observation that a fused group card can invite broad membership is logically reasonable. However, “splitting … needs pairwise scores … and a clustering step” names one possible approach, not a proven necessity. No split design needs to be selected in this review. [Plan:70](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-10-25-retrieval-poc/rerank-grouping-plan.md:70)

**Line 71 — “an estimate from the old repository’s measurements.”**

**Correction:** call it an **untested hypothesis**, without importing the old percentages as expected membership performance. There is no measured transfer relationship between those tasks. The old role score also does not establish an identity ceiling. [Plan:71](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-10-25-retrieval-poc/rerank-grouping-plan.md:71), [Old evidence labels](/Users/lchingen/tn-hivemind/evals/bench-v1/SPEC.md:71), [Old tagging questions](/Users/lchingen/tn-hivemind/src/tn_hivemind/data/relations.py:568)

**Line 71 — calibrated probabilities imply “the cascade is the design”; otherwise “only a recall-side filter.”**

**Correction:** calibration alone cannot select the architecture. The relevant quantities also include task errors, coverage, and the cost of a wrong action. Poor calibration does not logically make filtering safe; the old Jev mode reduced positive recall. [Plan:71](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-10-25-retrieval-poc/rerank-grouping-plan.md:71), [Old recall results:87–96](/Users/lchingen/tn-hivemind/evals/bench-x1/results/links-test-final.json:87), [Ranking calibration research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.04356)

**Line 72 — every related-but-different pair ranks near the top; without the gate it “would merge.”**

**Correction:** neither outcome follows automatically. Rank order depends on the model and candidates; merging depends on the consuming decision rule. The correct point is that relevance alone cannot establish identity. The predicted “2 of 3” source-assisted result is a hypothesis, not a measured accuracy estimate. [Plan:72](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-10-25-retrieval-poc/rerank-grouping-plan.md:72), [Retrieve-and-rerank distinction](https://sbert.net/examples/sentence_transformer/applications/retrieve_rerank/README.html)

**Line 74 — determinism “alone removes” membership variation.**

**Correction:** fixed scorer output can remove one source of variation for fixed inputs. It cannot remove variation caused by changing extracted cards, quotes, candidate lists, or later decisions. The proposed arms themselves distinguish different inputs. [Plan:61,74](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-10-25-retrieval-poc/rerank-grouping-plan.md:61)

### Section 6: proposed pipeline effect

**Line 78 — “Nothing in extraction’s contract.”**

**Correction:** the extraction schema might remain unchanged, but final membership authority expands when another component can add groups. This is a product behavior change under D149/D166, not merely an implementation detail. [Plan:78](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-10-25-retrieval-poc/rerank-grouping-plan.md:78), [D149](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS.md:2170), [D166](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS.md:2323)

**Line 78 — “model citation ∪ alias hit ∪ reranker hit.”**

**Correction:** this union can add memberships but cannot remove an existing wrong model or alias membership. Consequently, it cannot by itself deliver the earlier promised rejection of all forbidden memberships. This follows directly from the proposed set operation. [Plan:70,78](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-10-25-retrieval-poc/rerank-grouping-plan.md:78)

**Line 78 — identity uses the model “in the abstain band.”**

**Correction:** this implies another component decides identity outside that band, contradicting line 30’s “Jev is the check” positioning. The owner must choose which authority is intended before the POC is described as a route to implementation. [Plan:30,62,78](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-10-25-retrieval-poc/rerank-grouping-plan.md:30)

## 4. Literature on the positioning

### Is retrieval followed by a closed-set pair classifier recognized?

**Yes.** Dense or lexical retrieval can produce a shortlist, after which a model reads both sides and estimates a task-specific relation. Sentence Transformers documents retrieval followed by cross-encoder relevance scoring. Entity matching commonly calls candidate reduction **blocking**, then applies pair classification; Ditto is a clear example. [Retrieve and rerank](https://sbert.net/examples/sentence_transformer/applications/retrieve_rerank/README.html), [Ditto](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.00584)

A classifier and a reranker are not mutually exclusive categories. Sorting candidate pairs by the probability of the desired class makes the classifier act as a reranker. Applying a threshold then adds an acceptance decision. Probability-based ranking has a substantial literature, including explicit analysis of calibration and uncertainty. [Penha and Hauff](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.04356)

There is also a close grouping precedent: Saravanakumar et al. combine document–cluster similarity with a neural decision about joining an existing cluster or creating another. Their representation is not the exact Jev card-pair design, so this supports the general pattern rather than validating this implementation. [Event-driven news clustering](https://aclanthology.org/2021.eacl-main.198.pdf)

### What performance ranges have been reported?

These metrics are deliberately kept separate. **Accuracy, pairwise F1, and clustering F1 are not interchangeable.**

| Task | Published result | Relevance and limitation |
|---|---|---|
| Duplicate-question detection, QQP | BERT-base **71.2 F1**, BERT-large **72.1 F1** on the official GLUE test evaluation | Task-trained pair classifiers; Table 1 explicitly reports F1 for QQP. These are not Jev forecasts. [BERT, Table 1](https://aclanthology.org/N19-1423.pdf) |
| Entity matching | Ditto: **75.58 F1** on Amazon–Google, **94.37** on Beer, **98.99** on DBLP–ACM, **100.00** on Fodors–Zagats | Wide dataset variation despite the same general method. These are trained matching systems, not generic relevance scores. [Ditto, Table 5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.00584) |
| News-event clustering | Compared systems span **89.76–94.76 B-cubed F1**; the authors’ full system reaches **94.76** | Their dense-only variant reaches **68.98**, demonstrating that representation and task definition matter. These are event clusters, not overlapping thesis memberships. [News clustering, Table 1](https://aclanthology.org/2021.eacl-main.198.pdf) |

The literature supports **testing the pattern**. It does not support an expected accuracy number for this repository without its own accepted labels and evaluation.

### Known failure modes

- **Part-of versus same.** Event-coreference research explicitly distinguishes full identity from subevent relations. That supports keeping containment separate instead of treating it as weaker identity. [Araki et al.](https://aclanthology.org/L14-1725/)
- **Temporal differences.** The news-clustering paper reports incorrect merges without temporal information. In entity linking, source dates can exclude otherwise plausible namesakes. [News clustering](https://aclanthology.org/2021.eacl-main.198.pdf), [Historical entity linking](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10462-024-11102-9)
- **Popularity bias.** Historical entity-linking experiments measure systems preferring more popular entities over less common correct ones. This is evidence of a general risk, not a measured Jev defect on company stories. [Graciotti et al., Table 10](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10462-024-11102-9)
- **Similar wording with different identity.** Ditto’s examples include nearly identical product descriptions whose edition or grade changes the correct answer, and differently worded descriptions that identify the same product. [Ditto](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.00584)
- **Uncalibrated confidence.** Neural rankers can rank usefully while their numerical scores remain unreliable as probabilities. Conversely, calibration does not repair an incorrectly defined label. [Ranker calibration](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.04356), [Classifier calibration](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v70/guo17a.html)
- **Jev-specific boundaries.** TypeSafe’s 1.13 guidance warns about numerical/date reasoning, indirection, distracting context, and option-order effects. These support keeping explicit numerical conflicts in code and measuring semantic judgments on the actual task. They are not quantified 1.14 failure rates. [Jev 1.13 limitations](https://docs.typesafe.ai/model-jaggedness/jev-1.13)

### Choice, Score, or one question per call?

For the plan’s unordered relation labels, **Choice is the appropriate starting type**. A binary membership question could use Noul; retaining an explicit insufficient-information category makes Choice reasonable. Score is appropriate only when the owner-defined property is genuinely ordered. The vendor’s entity example shows Score is possible, not mandatory. [Choice](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/choice), [Score](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/score), [Entity example](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/entity_alignment)

Neither the API nor the old repository establishes a general requirement for one question per call. The old tagger already batches three. The important distinction is **one clearly defined judgment per question**, with the facts that judgment needs—not one HTTP request per judgment. [Old tagger:568–577](/Users/lchingen/tn-hivemind/src/tn_hivemind/data/relations.py:568), [Fan-out](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/fan-out)

## 5. Decisions only the owner can make

1. **What counts as belonging to the matter?**  
   In particular, decide the capex boundary and whether the existing broad group is itself acceptable. The prompt currently contains conflicting answers. My lean: settle the gold definition before interpreting model errors. [Plan:38,70,82](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-10-25-retrieval-poc/rerank-grouping-plan.md:38)

2. **What may Jev change automatically?**  
   Ranking candidates, flagging disagreements, adding memberships, and declaring identity are different authorities. My lean: evaluate membership directly, while keeping identity advisory unless a separate identity result justifies changing its authority. The old measurements do not settle this choice. [Plan:30,62,78](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-10-25-retrieval-poc/rerank-grouping-plan.md:62), [Old results](/Users/lchingen/tn-hivemind/docs/BENCHMARK.md:190)

3. **Which errors matter enough to block adoption?**  
   Wrongly joining a group, missing a valid group, and wrongly merging two quantities have different consequences. The owner sets those acceptance priorities; the numerical threshold is then selected on dev. My lean: do not reuse 0.95 merely because an old, different task used it. [Old policy:595–618](/Users/lchingen/tn-hivemind/src/tn_hivemind/data/relations.py:595), [Threshold guidance](https://docs.typesafe.ai/confidence)

4. **Whether to commission the paid POC after these corrections.**  
   The current pipeline should remain the unchanged control. Any model version used should be explicit, and account readiness should be verified rather than inferred from an old payment incident. This review neither spends the proposed budget nor changes a default. [Plan:61,83–84](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-10-25-retrieval-poc/rerank-grouping-plan.md:61), [Historical payment record](/Users/lchingen/tn-hivemind/docs/IMPLEMENTATION_LOG.md:91)

content.content:
1	# 让向量只找候选，让字段和判官定身份
2	
3	观点库只该让 embedding 做一件事：高召回地捞出"可能相关的已有观点"。"是不是同一个观点、该 skip（只加证据）、merge 还是新建"，要由代码比较结构化字段（标的、驱动、方向、财期或事件日期），再加一次"从几个排好序的候选里选一个"的 LLM 判定来决定。同一件事被多家报道，要先聚成事件簇，每簇只记一次证据。证据很一致。单向量模型在否定对比检索上最好只有 39%（随机为 25%）；在只差一个数字的金融句子上平均 54%（随机为 50%），四位数（也就是年份）处于随机水平。所以项目内部测到的"同一句话、不同季度 cosine 0.988"是预料之中的系统性行为，不是偶然。在实体匹配上，让 LLM 一次看完约 4 个候选再"选择"，比逐对判"是否相同"的 F1 高约 17 点，成本还更低。agent 记忆系统的演化指向同一方向：Mem0 在 2026 年 4 月放弃了让 LLM 在相似邻域上 UPDATE/DELETE；Graphiti 从不删除，只由代码按日期置失效；独立测评显示，这类系统的主要失败是漏更新（遗漏率 52–98%），而不是错更新。嵌入本身很便宜，每天 3,000 份文件全部分块嵌入，估计每月 4–45 美元；2 万条观点全部重嵌不到 1 美元。钱和风险都在判官调用和验证集上。没有任何公开基准测过"投资观点是否与已有观点相同"，所以下文推荐方案里的阈值、top-k 和事件时间窗，都只能在项目自己存储的数据上标定。
4	
5	## 记忆系统两年内从"改写与删除"退到"只追加、打失效标记"
6	
7	### Mem0 先让 LLM 增删改，再亲手拆掉
8	
9	Mem0 论文（2025 年 4 月）描述的是被模仿最多的两段式流水线。第一次 LLM 调用从对话里抽出事实。第二次对每条事实用向量取 top s=10 条最相似的记忆，让 GPT-4o-mini 通过 function calling 直接选操作：没有语义等价记忆时 ADD，有补充信息时 UPDATE，被新信息反驳时 DELETE，否则 NOOP。中间没有单独的分类器 ([Mem0 paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2504.19413))。开源代码 v1.0.11 实际每条事实只取 `limit=5`，调用前把 UUID 映射成 "0""1"……"for handling UUID hallucinations"。UPDATE 在同一 id 下覆盖文本和向量。DELETE 直接从向量库硬删，旧值只留在一张检索从不读取的 SQLite 历史表里 ([mem0 v1.0.11 main.py](https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/blob/v1.0.11/mem0/memory/main.py#L555-L592); [L1340-L1364](https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/blob/v1.0.11/mem0/memory/main.py#L1340-L1364))。提示词用例子划边界："Likes cheese pizza" 与 "Loves cheese pizza" 不更新；"cheese pizza" 加 "chicken pizza" 被合并改写成一句；"Loves" 遇上 "Dislikes" 就 DELETE ([mem0 prompts.py](https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/blob/0724291bd864cf807e88ee8981c8226644e8fb42/mem0/configs/prompts.py#L176-L325))。图变体 Mem0g 后来把删关系改成了软删除（`r.valid = false, r.invalidated_at`），理由是要支持对历史状态做时间推理 ([graph_memory.py](https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/blob/v1.0.11/mem0/memory/graph_memory.py#L420-L432))。
10	
11	**2026-04-14，Mem0 把整套流水线换掉了。** 新算法只追加（"nothing is overwritten or deleted"），检索改成语义 + BM25 + 实体加权的混合打分。官方给的理由是旧算法的 UPDATE/DELETE 会丢历史、处理"信息变了"很差：用户从纽约搬到旧金山，两条事实都应该带着时间保留下来 ([Mem0 migration v2→v3](https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/blob/0724291bd864cf807e88ee8981c8226644e8fb42/docs/migration/platform-v2-to-v3.mdx))。现在的开源写入路径是：整批新消息嵌入后只取 top_k=10 条已有记忆，一次 LLM 调用抽取新记忆，机械去重只有 MD5 精确文本比对 ([main.py L918-L1220](https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/blob/0724291bd864cf807e88ee8981c8226644e8fb42/mem0/memory/main.py#L918-L1220))。语义去重完全交给提示词里的两句话："语义等价且没有新上下文就跳过"，"拿不准就抽，下游去重系统会处理真重复" ([prompts.py L468-L946](https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/blob/0724291bd864cf807e88ee8981c8226644e8fb42/mem0/configs/prompts.py#L468-L946))。研究笔记读代码时还发现，模型返回的 `linked_memory_ids`（包括标"矛盾"的链接）在 Python 开源路径里根本没有写入存储 ([main.py L1007-L1200](https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/blob/0724291bd864cf807e88ee8981c8226644e8fb42/mem0/memory/main.py#L1007-L1200))。真正的冲突处理搬进了闭源平台的 "Dream" 层。Supersede 把被反驳的旧事实标成过时，并链接到新事实。Merge 把重复折叠进一条规范记忆，被合并的记录默认对读取隐藏，但保留不删，原话是 "Nothing Dream does is destructive" ([dream.mdx](https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/blob/0724291bd864cf807e88ee8981c8226644e8fb42/docs/platform/features/dream.mdx))。Dream 的提示词、候选数和阈值都没有公开，也没有精度或召回数字。
12	
13	Mem0 的效果数字全部是厂商自报，而且有争议。论文表格里 LoCoMo 的 LLM-judge 分数是 Mem0 66.88、Mem0g 68.44、Zep 65.99、LangMem 58.10、A-Mem 48.38，但**全上下文的 72.90 高于所有记忆系统** ([Mem0 paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2504.19413))。Zep 指出 Mem0 有三处配置错误，比如把两个说话人都设成 user；纠正后 Zep 自报 75.14 ([Zep blog](https://www.getzep.com/blog/lies-damn-lies-statistics-is-mem0-really-sota-in-agent-memory/))。Letta 用一个只带 grep、打开文件这类工具的普通 agent 跑出 74.0% ([Letta blog](https://www.letta.com/blog/benchmarking-ai-agent-memory))。v3 自报 LoCoMo 91.6、LongMemEval 93.4，没有找到独立复现 ([Mem0 changelog](https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/blob/0724291bd864cf807e88ee8981c8226644e8fb42/docs/changelog/highlights.mdx))。对观点库来说，这些问答分数用处不大，因为它们测的是回答问题，不是"这一条是否重复"的判断。
14	
15	### Graphiti 用结构定候选，一次调用出两张下标表，日期交给代码
16	
17	Graphiti 是 Zep 的开源核心，也是"不删、只失效"做得最完整的公开参考，候选生成和判定拆得最干净。去重候选按结构定：只在**同一对实体之间**的边里找，先用 BM25 + cosine 混合检索（RRF 融合，默认取 10 条，cosine 下限 0.6），再按端点精确过滤。矛盾候选是在整个 group 里不加端点过滤再搜一次，并扣掉已经是去重候选的那些 ([edge_operations.py L399-L646](https://github.com/getzep/graphiti/blob/d50741d1bf463cbe3859eb73914cbff1b66839e6/graphiti_core/utils/maintenance/edge_operations.py#L399-L646); [search_config.py](https://github.com/getzep/graphiti/blob/d50741d1bf463cbe3859eb73914cbff1b66839e6/graphiti_core/search/search_config.py))。如果新事实的文本和端点与已有边逐字相同，就直接复用旧边，把新 episode 的 uuid 追加进 `episodes` 来源列表，不调用 LLM ([edge_operations.py L864-L1087](https://github.com/getzep/graphiti/blob/d50741d1bf463cbe3859eb73914cbff1b66839e6/graphiti_core/utils/maintenance/edge_operations.py#L864-L1087))。这是"重复报道只加来源"最便宜的实现。其余情况交给一次 small 模型调用，同时返回 `duplicate_facts` 和 `contradicted_facts` 两个下标列表，代码丢弃越界的下标。提示词明令："数值、日期或关键限定词有差异，就不算重复"；"不能仅凭时间更近、日期不同，或同一批实体出现了新事件，就推断矛盾" ([dedupe_edges.py](https://github.com/getzep/graphiti/blob/d50741d1bf463cbe3859eb73914cbff1b66839e6/graphiti_core/prompts/dedupe_edges.py))。
18	
19	谁失效，由确定性代码按两条时间线决定。`valid_at`/`invalid_at` 是事实在世界上成立的区间，`created_at`/`expired_at` 是系统何时得知、何时让它退役。被反驳的旧边得到 `invalid_at = 新边.valid_at`。如果矛盾候选的 `valid_at` 反而比新边晚，说明新到的这条才是旧消息（乱序到达），这时把新边的 `invalid_at` 设成候选的 `valid_at`。区间不重叠的一概不动，什么都不删 ([edge_operations.py L715-L783](https://github.com/getzep/graphiti/blob/d50741d1bf463cbe3859eb73914cbff1b66839e6/graphiti_core/utils/maintenance/edge_operations.py#L715-L783))。还有一个可以直接搬来用的细节是未来时守卫：含 "plans to / expects to / scheduled to" 的事实，`valid_at` 夹到陈述日；"by / before" 这样的截止日期不当作失效日 ([temporal_edge_utils.py](https://github.com/getzep/graphiti/blob/d50741d1bf463cbe3859eb73914cbff1b66839e6/graphiti_core/utils/maintenance/temporal_edge_utils.py))。实体解析同样确定性优先：精确名和 MinHash（Jaccard ≥ 0.9）先判，只有低熵名称和多重匹配才交给 LLM；cosine 候选 15 条、下限 0.6，不重排 ([node_operations.py](https://github.com/getzep/graphiti/blob/d50741d1bf463cbe3859eb73914cbff1b66839e6/graphiti_core/utils/maintenance/node_operations.py); [dedup_helpers.py](https://github.com/getzep/graphiti/blob/d50741d1bf463cbe3859eb73914cbff1b66839e6/graphiti_core/utils/maintenance/dedup_helpers.py))。它的弱点也很具体。批量导入 `add_episode_bulk` 跳过了失效处理，所以矛盾检测依赖逐条按顺序摄入 ([bulk_utils.py](https://github.com/getzep/graphiti/blob/d50741d1bf463cbe3859eb73914cbff1b66839e6/graphiti_core/utils/bulk_utils.py))。在 MemoryAgentBench 的事实合并单跳任务上，Zep 只有 **7.0** 分，远低于纯 BM25 的 48.0 ([MemoryAgentBench](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.05257))：只认显式矛盾的保守规则，漏掉了隐式替代。
20	
21	### 其余系统：要么自由改写、要么按名字哈希，少数把冲突当成记录
22	
23	其余系统大致分三类。第一类让 agent 自由改写记忆文本，但不一定留历史。Letta 已把 MemGPT 式的记忆工具换成 git 仓库里的 markdown 文件，"every change to memory is automatically versioned"，另有"defragmentation"技能合并重复，但没有给出任何测量 ([Letta blog](https://www.letta.com/blog/context-repositories))。LangMem 默认允许插入和更新、关闭删除，更新就是同一 key 下 `store.put` 覆盖，没有版本 ([langmem extraction.py](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langmem/blob/48e3c11f5bb527282c7d5339c6a87a0b35abccfc/src/langmem/knowledge/extraction.py))。A-MEM 每加一条取 k=5 个近邻，让 LLM 改写邻居的标签和上下文；研究笔记读代码发现，它把检索结果里的排名位置当成了存储下标，库里超过 k 条之后就会改错笔记 ([A-mem memory_system.py](https://github.com/agiresearch/A-mem/blob/ceffb860f0712bbae97b184d440df62bc910ca8d/agentic_memory/memory_system.py))。第二类按确定性身份去重。Cognee 的节点 id 是规范化名称的 uuid5 ([generate_node_id.py](https://github.com/topoteretes/cognee/blob/37f788bd287750e10d7610173e5332b3843f6ebd/cognee/infrastructure/engine/utils/generate_node_id.py))，便宜，但同名的不同事物会被并成一个，相当于"值相等即同一身份"。第三类少数系统把冲突当成一等记录，最贴近观点库。Cognee 的 `review_conflicts` 由代码按"同关系名 + 共享一个端点"构造候选组，LLM 把每个冲突标成 `time_varying`（后来的来源可以合法地给出不同值）或 `fixed`（只可能有一个真值，不同就说明有一方错了），只记录争议、不改事实，"值只是计划或提议时不算冲突"，并写明"Omitting a conflict is the safe outcome" ([review_conflicts.txt](https://github.com/topoteretes/cognee/blob/37f788bd287750e10d7610173e5332b3843f6ebd/cognee/infrastructure/llm/prompts/review_conflicts.txt))。Hindsight 的观点网络给每条观点一个置信度，新事实按 reinforce / weaken / contradict 加减 α 或 2α ([Hindsight](https://arxiv.org/html/2512.12818v1))。MemoryOS 则按容量淘汰：长期知识是 `deque(maxlen=100)`，最老的被静默丢掉 ([MemoryOS long_term.py](https://github.com/BAI-LAB/MemoryOS/blob/587ed7755c7aed179965792830ff1b5ad9a6fa92/memoryos-pypi/long_term.py))。
